newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes firmer despite a rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes firmer despite a rate cut.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev firmed to around 1,501-1,502 per dollar at close on Friday from the morning's 1,503-1,506 as investors opted for local debt paper despite a cut in the main interest rate, dealers said.
"The lev edged up as investors continued to sell foreign currency for levs to lock into higher-yielding government securities despite the rate cut," a bank dealer said.
The local currency fell by around six levs against the German mark from the morning to 884-886 per mark at the close, tracking the mark rise against the dollar on international markets, traders said.

Dollar trade accounts for 45 percent of the local forex market daily turnover and the lev exchange rates for other major currencies are adjusted to their spot rates against the dollar on international markets.
The Bulgarian National Bank on Thursday cut its main interest rate to 5.2 percent monthly from 6.2 percent now. The new rate becomes effective from Monday, May 12.

Local and foreign investors have been actively selling foreign currency for levs to buy high-yield local debt paper since March as Bulgaria's macroeconomic performance improved and the lev stabilised after an interim cabinet took office.
